# Section

Figma: [07h. Section](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-949) · Family: 07 Cards & Lists · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

The section header: a heading that labels a region of a screen - placed above a card row, a list or any content block. Title + optional supporting line + an optional trailing “See all” action + optional leading icon and divider. Size (Lg / Md / Sm) × Direction.

### Section

Section header that titles a region of a screen (above a carousel, card row or list) with optional description, leading icon, divider and a See all action. It is a heading, not a row and not a container.

Level: molecule · Contains: Button

Use when:
- Titling a deals carousel or updates strip with a See all jump
- Organising long screens into primary sections (Size=Lg) and sub-sections (Size=Md/Sm)

Don't use when:
- Collapsible content: use Accordion
- Rows: use ListItem
- The small header inside a grouped list: use ActionList Has header
- Screen title: use AppBar

Accessibility: Map Size to heading level (Lg h2, Md h3, Sm h4); See all link names its target (See all deals); hide it when nothing more exists.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Section organizes a screen into titled regions. It is not a list row (ListItem) and it is bigger than the small overline inside ActionList - it is the standalone heading you place above carousels, card rows and lists, with an optional “See all” jump. The lineup reads: Section (titles a region) → ActionList / List (the container) → ListItem / SelectRow (the rows).

### Anatomy & slots

Title is required; description, the “See all” action, a leading accent icon, and a bottom divider are each optional.

Title + action

+ description

+ leading icon + divider

Title only (no action)

### Sizes

Lg for primary page sections (~20), Md for sub-sections (~16), Sm for minor groupings (~14).

Lg · page section

Md · sub-section

Sm · minor group

### Direction - LTR & RTL

The action moves to the leading edge and the chevron flips; the title/description right-align in Arabic.

LTR

RTL

### Examples in context

A Section titles the region directly beneath it - a carousel, a card grid, or a list.

### Code examples

Flutter usage of Section.

### Section with “See all”

```dart
SafqahSection(
  size: SectionSize.lg,
  title: 'Your deals',
  description: '12 active investments',
  leadingIcon: SafqahIcons.trendingUp,
  action: SectionAction(label: 'See all', onTap: () => context.push('/deals')),
)
```

### Plain sub-section

```dart
SafqahSection(
  size: SectionSize.md,
  title: 'Recent activity',
  showDivider: true,
)
```

### Usage - Do & Don’t

Do

Use a Section to title a region and offer a “See all” jump to its full view.

Don’t

Don’t use Section as a list row or for body copy - it’s a heading, not content (use ListItem / body text).

Do

Match size to hierarchy - Lg for page sections, Md for sub-sections, Sm for minor groups.

Don’t

Don’t show “See all” when there’s nothing more to see, and don’t stack two competing Lg headers in one view.
